2026 Paris Motor Show • OMODA 4 Lands in Paris To Showcase Futuristic Styling, Looks Like a Discount Urus
JLR North America Recalls Nearly 94,000 Range Rover Vehicles Over Failing Rearview Cameras
9 photos
Photo: Land Rover
Jaguar Land Rover's North American subsidiary has identified a potential issue affecting 93,997 units of the Range Rover. Affected 2022 through 2026 models were produced in Solihull for the US between July 8, 2021, and June 4, 2026. Solihull is the flagship manufacturing facility of the company, and Solihull also served as the home of the Land Rover Series and the body-on-frame Defender.
The drain holes for the rearview cameras in the subject Range Rover sport utility vehicles aren't enough to let water and moisture escape. If water pools where it shouldn't, the electric and electronic bits of the rearview camera slowly die, and that's not okay by National Highway Traffic Safety Administration standards.
Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 111 covers all things rear visibility. While it may not explicitly guarantee that rearview camera parts will never break down over the span of the vehicle, FMVSS 111 does outlaw backup cameras from not displaying the rearview image when reverse is selected. Such failures and even the occasional intermittent glitch mean the vehicle legally fails compliance.
JLR North America estimates that 100 percent of the recall population carries the defect, conceding that five model years of the US-market Range Rover need replacement cameras. The tailgate's water management system is described in the recall documentation as potentially insufficient, allowing water to pool around the rearview camera installation. This water generates a few headaches, naturally.
In the first instance, moisture or water causes a distorted image. The worst-case scenario is no rearview image at all, increasing the risk of a crash or an injury. Care to guess how many claims and field reports JLR North America has logged so far? Make that 2,295 such claims and reports in the United States from August 3, 2022, through September 28, 2026.
Photo: Land Rover The safety boffins are not aware of any accident or injury reports. Jaguar Land Rover 's Product Safety and Compliance Committee opened an investigation back on July 31, 2026, prompted by anomalous rearview camera replacement rates on the current-gen Range Rover. Global warranty data had flagged an elevated replacement rate in Canada and the United States market, a rate no other market matched.
This, in turn, meant that a dedicated team was tasked with manually reviewing every claim for clues. The review ran through September 2026. Removed camera assemblies were shipped to the supplier for teardown analysis. Back in August, a separate camera recall affecting the Discovery line spurred the decision forum to ask for harder field evidence that the replacements were genuine failures rather than warranty noise.
On September 18, the committee was informed that a new process requiring evidence before approval of camera replacements had produced a significant decrease in claim rate. What that says about the pre-September 2026 claims is a question the recall filing published by the NHTSA unfortunately does not answer. The supplier ultimately told JLR that returned cameras had failed from water ingress.
This is the second time since 2024 the Range Rover has faced this problem. A separate campaign from two years ago covered 11,961 units of the fifth-gen model, specifically Range Rovers built from March 2022 to December 2023. That said, Jaguar Land Rover corrected the water ingress problem in production with the introduction of a revised seal for the tailgate trim piece housing the camera.
Dealers will be notified later in October 2026 with instructions to drill additional drain holes in the underside of the tailgate trim containing the camera. The functionality of the camera will be verified. If required, a replacement is on the menu. Interim customer notifications are due on December 11, 2026, but JLR North America has yet to finalize the planned remedy owner notification date.

2026 Paris Motor Show • 2027 Hyundai Bayon Finally Looks More Like a Box and Less Like an Egg
Tesla Roadster Uses New 4680 Cells That Promise To Fix Everything That's Wrong With the Cybertruck
57 photos
Photo: Hagerty via YouTube
One of the most intriguing aspects of the refreshed Tesla Roadster is its 4680-cell battery pack. The format hasn't made the Cybertruck a fan favorite, mostly due to its poor charging performance. However, Tesla promised that the Roadster will feature the fastest-charging battery the company has ever made. Information is scarce, but here's what's different on the Roadster's battery compared to the Cybertruck.
For many, especially those who have not been following Tesla closely, the Roadster will forever be associated with the flying demonstration that broke the internet on October 15. Even my daughter, who doesn't care about almost anything, sent me an Instagram reel of the demo. That's a significant change, because, most of the time, Tesla videos live a short and miserable life inside Tesla bubbles on X, and rarely make the news, especially positive news.
However, the Roadster is much more than a flying (albeit briefly) car. If Tesla finally starts production (which in itself is a big IF), it will begin with the street-legal Performance variant, which almost-normal people will be able to buy. For them, almost-normal concerns like range and charging time will be more important than the answer to the question, "but does it fly?" And the crucial answers depend on the Roadster's most important part: the battery.
Tesla's 4680 cells: The dream, the promise, the reality check Years ago, when Tesla was still a religion, and Musk was the patriarch, Tesla promised that a new battery type would change everything. The larger cell, with a 4680 format (46 mm in diameter and 80 mm tall), was the highlight of the 2020 Battery Day . On stage, Musk promised that the new battery would hold five times the capacity of a 2170 cell and deliver six times the power.
At the time, Tesla had just bought Maxwell, which developed the dry electrode process for its supercapacitors. Musk was confident Tesla could use the technology for its battery cells. The dry battery electrode (DBE) process could significantly cut cell production time and costs. However, it was difficult to master in volume production, which crippled Tesla battery program.
Photo: YouTube screenshot Besides DBE, Tesla also considered improved chemistry, with a high-nickel cathode and a silicon anode. In the end, none of these promising technologies have proved easy to deploy. This failure has made Tesla's 4680 cells just larger variants of their 2170 counterpart, with the added disadvantage of being heat traps, very difficult to cool in a pack.
This has become obvious once Tesla installed the 4680 cells in a car, the 2023 Model Y AWD built in Austin. People who bought that car, believing in Elon Musk's promises at the Battery Day, were utterly disappointed by the poor charging performance. Tesla admitted defeat less than a year later, in September 2023, when it canceled the 4680 Model Y. However, it still started deliveries of the Cybertruck in November 2023 using 4680 cells.
Tesla Cybertruck: The second victim of the failed 4680 cells When Elon Musk announced that the Cybertruck would use 4680 cells, almost everyone was disappointed. However, Tesla insisted that the Cybertruck would use new cells with improved characteristics. The second-generation 4680 cells were dubbed "Cybercells" and promised 10% higher energy density, thus being roughly on par with 2170 cells in this regard.
However, as the Cybertruck started deliveries in November 2023, customers noticed that adding the word "cyber" to everything doesn't necessarily change things for the better. The 4680 cells were still the weak link in the Cybertruck's performance, and the Cybercell moniker could not change that. Charging a Cybertruck still sucked, with owners reporting 35 minutes or more to charge from 10% to 80%.
Photo: Tesla on YouTube Tesla improved the situation somehow in 2024 with a software update, promising that 800-volt Tesla Superchargers would shorten the charging time. It did, but not by much. Owners would have to start charging their trucks below 5% SoC to see a meaningful improvement. Up to today, the Cybertruck has one of the least efficient charging curves of all the EVs on the market.
The Roadster is the third Tesla EV using 4680 cells. Is third time a charm? During the Roadster demo event on October 15, we learned that the new show car and future sports car (if it launches) also uses 4680 cells. Now, for everyone who followed Tesla closely for the past five years, that's a bad omen. However, Tesla pinky-swears that this time it will be different, and the Roadster would change everything we know about Tesla's 4680 cells.
Photo: Hagerty via YouTube We have little detail, but Tesla's chief of engineering Lars Moravy offered some clues in an interview with Hagerty. He said that the Roadster uses "special cells" with a special chemistry and, undoubtedly, special characteristics. He didn't call them "Roadcells" to match the car's name, as he did with the Cybertruck. What's certain is that they only exist on the Roadster's spec sheet for now.
Moravy did not talk about the cells' chemistry, which is why I believe nothing's changed on that front. Instead, he pointed to small optimizations, and all address the Cybertruck's major issue: bad thermals. Aluminum cans are used instead of steel, which Moravy said is better at dissipating heat. Aluminum also makes the battery pack lighter, same as the titanium upper plate.
However, the most visible change is using a cooling system with double-sided cooling jackets. This ensures that every single cell is surrounded by cooling lines that provide a uniform heat flux throughout the pack. This should address the thermal limitations of 4680 cells, which were obvious in all previous vehicles that used them.
The Tesla Roadster might need more than special 4680 cells to succeed For anyone following Tesla's motorsport achievements, and especially Unplugged Performance's result at Pikes Peak and other famous races, battery thermals are crucial. The Roadster does take some steps to ensure that the 4680 cells don't run into thermal limitations even during the most demanding race sessions. Or so Tesla promised.
Photo: Tesla Lard Moravy said that Roadster owners should be able to push the car to the limits for up to 20 minutes on a racetrack. This might not sound like enough, but anyone who has driven a car on a racetrack knows the toll 20 minutes of spirited driving can take on the driver. At the end of the session, the Roadster should be able to charge from 10% to 80% in no more than 10 minutes.
That would make the Roadster the fastest-charging Tesla ever produced, if Moravy's estimate is correct. However, I'd take that with a grain of salt: Moravy has a long history of exaggerating performance, perhaps even more than his outspoken boss. He also promised that the Cybertruck would charge much faster than it does. Sometimes, people wonder if Tesla executives ever charge their cars. That is, if they drive a Tesla to begin with.

2026 Paris Motor Show • Ford Rolls Out the Ranger MS-RT Champion Edition: You Can Choose Any Color As Long as It Is Black
Volkswagen Facing January 2027 Workers' Strike in Germany as Wage Talks Collapse
8 photos
Photo: Volkswagen
The Volkswagen Group's restructuring plan has run into what can only be described as the only force that is capable of stopping production in the Wolfsburg-based automaker's home market. IG Metall, namely the labor union representing a great deal of Volkswagen Group workers in Germany, claims the company must reverse last month's termination of nearly all wage agreements.
IG Metall's deadline is the end of October 2026. If wage talks do collapse, workers aren't shying away from striking en masse. Strikes would kick off in January 2027, and such developments would undeniably hurt Volkswagen both at home and in the rest of the world. The dispute, however, turns on more than just wages.
VW's decision reopened working hours, holiday pay, and other long-standing employment terms that German workers had treated as fixed parts of their jobs. For a manufacturer trying to aggressively cut costs across its German workforce, that is a dangerous place to start. IG Metall's position is pretty straightforward.
The union wants to restore the agreements, then talk. Volkswagen is equally direct. More to the point, all the conditions that shaped the 2024 collective bargaining agreement have deteriorated too far for the automaker to leave said terms untouched. Management's argument comes in the form of financial pressure, with Volkswagen targeting 20 billion euros in cost reductions by 2030.
Another 11 billion euros are expected from lower overhead costs. All said targeted savings must come from somewhere, and labor remains an option. The restructuring behind the wage fight is more than just a pay negotiation. As you might have already heard, Volkswagen intends to eliminate 100,000 jobs. In the process, up to four German plants could be shuttered.
Photo: Volkswagen Easily the biggest-ever overhaul in Germany for Volkswagen, these reductions are driven by the expense of its EV strategy, Chinese newcomers, and tariff costs. The Volkswagen works council claims that Volkswagen's executive board could freeze salaries for up to 660,000 employees worldwide through 2030, yet the group has refused to comment on such measures.
The silence understandably shaped the union's response. When factory workers are being asked to accept lower labor costs without a complete picture of which production lines, assembly plants, and employment categories will absorb the cuts, it's hard to blame them for being angry at the suits in Wolfsburg.
IG Metall also notes that Volkswagen is retreating from commitments made in the 2024 agreement, whereas management argues that changed market conditions require new terms. A truce would prevent strikes before January 1st. Negotiations on the canceled agreements are planned to start on November 24, as reported by Reuters and confirmed by VW's media site.
Negotiations would kick off at the Emden plant, then continue on December 15 at the Zwickau complex. Both sit at the center of the automaker's EV strategy, making Emden and Zwickau both symbolic and practical locations for talks. If the group cannot stabilize labor costs at said facilities, the Hanover plant, and the Neckarsulm complex, the proposed transition plan becomes harder to fund.
IG Metall's threat is certainly credible because German automakers cannot easily replace skilled workers. For now, the two sides are prepping for different outcomes. A possible compromise already exists in VW's proposal for so-called transfer companies. With support from the federal employment agency, affected employees would be retrained and helped in finding employment outside VW.
Via // Reuters

New Hot Wheels Red Line Club Exclusive 240Z Looks Like Double the Trouble
17 photos
Photo: Mattel
One of my wife’s coworkers invited us to lunch today, and I knew I couldn’t go there empty handed. I asked if their son liked cars, thinking I’d give him one of my premium, carded Hot Wheels collectibles. I don’t think he liked it, as he seemed more like a FIFA enthusiast. Oh well, I know what I can get him the next time.
It can feel a bit mind boggling to see that most people don’t really care about tiny cars, especially when I’m so caught up in the topic on a daily basis. I guess kids these days don’t even pay attention to real-world vehicles either, as they’re just a means of transportation to them.
I’m not sure if I should blame the car companies, the ride-sharing companies or the Social Media platforms for the current situation. I assume identifying the “culprit” wouldn’t make a difference anyway. In a way, they’re probably better off this way, as this hobby can be quite expensive and time consuming.
That’s true if you do manage to pick your battles carefully. Take for instance what’s happening in the Red Line Club series. While Overdrive seemed like the perfect solution to a problem that has been a nuisance for years, it won’t guarantee you can get every single RLC on a yearly basis.
The introduction of the Chase cars has made the game even more complicated than before. We’ve seen three of them so far in 2026: the Porsche 911 Turbo 3.3 Targa, the 1948 Chevrolet Fleetline and the '21 Ford Bronco.
Buying all three of them from eBay could cost as much as $2,500, which seems downright insane if you ask me. The Bronco is the cheapest one of the bunch, and I expect the new Datsun 240Z will be quite a bit more desirable by comparison.
This is the same casting that Phil Riehlman designed for the 2006 First Edition collection, where it debuted alongside other memorable castings such as the Ferrari 512 M and the Bone Shaker. Yes, that’s right. This is the kind of RLC model that exists across multiple series, which means it doesn’t feature any opening parts.
That’s a huge downside to me, but I guess other people don’t mind the situation. Why would it still be in production after two decades otherwise? The 240Z first big moment happened in 2011 when it joined the Super Treasure Hunt series, and it went one step further in 2013 with only 3,500 units showing up for the HWC.com Special Edition release.
We have seen four other similarly variations since, and you might remember it even showed up as a replica of Larry Chen’s Ole Orange Bang earlier this year for Boulevard . While Spectraflame Aqua looks like a good match for the regular version of the RLC release, I’m not a fan of the lettered tires (which isn’t something I’d normally say).
Mattel will only be making 5,000 units of the Polished Chrome Chase, and this is one battle you might want to stay away from if you care about your sanity and your wallet. But hey, who am I to stop you from trying? The action starts on October 27 , 2026 at 9 AM PT, and you can only order two items per customer, for $28 a pop. I imagine it will all be over in under 60 seconds, so good luck with it.

source_document.body:
Storage
ADT R27A-BK3 top view
The ADT R27A-BK3 is an inexpensive way to add a U.2 NVMe SSD to a system that only has standard PCIe slots. We have been testing the EDSFF version of this adapter family , and we wanted to see how the U.2 variant works since it uses a different connector and drive form factor.
You can find what we purchased on Amazon (affiliate link) or AliExpress (Affiliate link) . There are different versions, including an EDSFF version we previously reviewed, so make sure you are buying the correct model.
ADT R27A-BK3 U.2 to PCIe Adapter Review
The metal shell is fairly large because it has to enclose a full-length U.2 drive, a blower fan, and the adapter PCB.
ADT R27A-BK3 top view
Along the top, there is just the metal cover. The shell provides structural support and helps direct airflow over the drive.
ADT R27A-BK3 side profile
The I/O plate mostly holds the card in place and provides vents for airflow.
ADT R27A-BK3 rear bracket
The rear of the unit has screws and a fan cable with a standard 4-pin PWM connector.
ADT R27A-BK3 rear with PWM fan connector
The bottom edge carries a PCIe Gen5 x4 gold-finger connector. ADT also sells a Gen4 version of this adapter, so check which generation you need before ordering.
ADT R27A-BK3 PCIe Gen5 x4 connector
Removing the cover requires a few screws, and then we can see what is inside.
ADT R27A-BK3 internal layout
First, there is the 4-pin PWM blower fan. The board is labeled as a PCIe x4-to-U.2 SSD adapter with an SFF-8639 connector.
ADT R27A-BK3 PWM blower fan
The adapter uses an SFF-8639 connector, which means it is designed for U.2 drives only. This is a key difference from the EDSFF version we reviewed earlier, which used an SFF-TA-1002 connector for E1.S and E3.S drives.
ADT R27A-BK3 with KIOXIA drive
Next, let us get some drives in the unit so you can see what this looks like. We used a Samsung PM9D3 U.2 SSD for testing.
ADT R27A-BK3 with Samsung PM9D3
The fan is important here because the drive sits inside an enclosed shell. In our testing, we did not see the same thermal throttling behavior we saw with the EDSFF version of this adapter.
ADT R27A-BK3 Performance
We tested two different drives in the ADT R27A-BK3 to see how it handles varying interface generations and thermal loads. The first drive is a Samsung MZQLB7T6HMLA-00007, which is a 7.68TB U.2 SSD using a PCIe Gen3 x4 interface.
Samsung PCIe Gen3 U.2 In Cheap R27 Adapter
During a 20-minute run, the Samsung drive peaked at 2,252 MB/s and sustained 2,179 MB/s. This represents a roughly 3.2% drop from peak to sustained performance. Throughput dropped slightly around the eight-minute mark but then held steady near 2.18 GB/s for the rest of the test. Temperature peaked at 78 C, staying well below the drive’s warning threshold of 86 C.
The second drive tested was a Solidigm D7-PS1010, also in a 7.68TB capacity but using a much faster PCIe Gen5 x4 interface. This test focused on sustained 128K sequential writes to stress the adapter and cooling solution under high bandwidth conditions.
Solidigm D7-PS1010 7.68TB in Low-Cost U.2 to PCIe Adapter
The Solidigm drive achieved a peak throughput of 7,946 MB/s and sustained 7,838 MB/s over the same 20-minute duration. The performance drop from peak to sustained was minimal at just 1.4%. While the chart shows brief dips in throughput, the drive quickly returned to approximately 7.8 GB/s. Temperature leveled off at 70 C, well below its warning threshold of 77 C.
Neither drive exhibited sustained thermal throttling during the 20-minute runs. Both drives remained below their respective warning temperature thresholds throughout the runs. So the cooling on this one isn’t too bad, but if you have a hotter drive, you might want to trust it, but verify it is working in your machine.
Final Words
The ADT R27A-BK3 is a straightforward way to add a U.2 NVMe drive to a system without native U.2 support. The included fan and metal shell help keep the drive cool, and we did not observe thermal throttling during our testing.
Just make sure you buy the correct version for your drive type. This R27A-BK3 is specifically for U.2 SFF-8639 drives, while the EDSFF variant uses a different connector and is sold under a different model number.

Photo: Instagram | stars.in.the.ceiling
The modern-day Dodge Charger still fails to attract real petrolheads, and that is due to a very simple reason: the lack of a V8 engine option.
However, that is about to change, as an eight-cylinder unit will finally make its way under the hood of the company’s new muscle car, as well as its four-door sibling. This will reportedly happen at the end of 2027, as that’s when production is expected to kick off, and it will start arriving at dealers for the 2028 model year. That is the plan, anyway, though let’s not forget that a lot could happen in the following year, so fingers crossed that we finally get a new-age Charger with V8 firepower.
Now, the latest Dodge Charger may not get that much attention from the gearhead crowd these days, but its predecessor still does, and so does its two-door sibling, the previous Challenger . And it is not hard to understand why, because these models were offered with V8 options, including the mighty 6.2-liter supercharged V8 lump that powered the numerous Hellcat versions that the company released over the years. And yes, this also includes the crazy Demon and Demon 170 versions of the old Challenger.
It is almost impossible to talk about the Hellcat family without reminding ourselves that the Dodge Challenger SRT Demon 170 remains the most powerful and fastest production muscle car ever made. It had as much as 1,025 horsepower in its top configuration, with E85 in the fuel tank, and 945 pound-feet (1,280 Nm) of torque, taking a neck-snapping 1.66 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph), and dealing with the standing quarter mile in 8.91 seconds, with an exit speed of just over 151 mph (243+ kph). All of that in a stock car!
Photo: Instagram | stars.in.the.ceiling Mind you, we aren’t here to remind you how cool the Demon 170 was (and still is), nor to talk about the Dodge Challenger / Charger SRT Hellcat models as a whole. Instead, what caught our eye was the Charger pictured above in the gallery, which came directly from Stars In The Ceiling. The tuner recently took to social media to release these pictures, announcing that the vehicle in question is owned by USC football star Waymond Jordan Jr.
The 22-year-old athlete, who turns 23 at the beginning of November, took his Dodge Charger SRT Hellcat to the quoted tuner for a makeover, which includes quite a few things. For instance, Stars In The Ceiling mentions the new stealth tundra exterior color, which was achieved via wrapping the four-door muscle car, and the exterior is adorned with a pair of black racing stripes that run across the vehicle’s entire length, and they are framed by the red lines.
A special decal can be seen on the rear doors, windows, rear three-quarter panels, and C-pillars, and the emblems on the front fenders and trunk lid now have a red look. The widebody kit appears to have come directly from the factory, and the alloys are not mentioned in the caption, and since we are not exactly wheel experts, we reckon they are probably the standard ones. But you may want to refrain from quoting us on that for obvious reasons.
Now, while this tuned Dodge Charger SRT Hellcat has a sandy look on the outside, joined by the black racing strips and red elements, including the Hellcat side decals, the cockpit is mostly red. We can see that the seats feature red leather upholstery and some white stitching here and there, and these have likely come like this straight from the factory.
Photo: Instagram | stars.in.the.ceiling However, the Alcantara upholstery is new, and we can see it on the steering wheel, save for the bottom part, as well as on the headliner, and probably on other elements that are simply not visible in these pictures. The tuner is not called Stars In The Ceiling for nothing, because this four-door muscle car also feature a starry sky headliner that is part of the makeover.
As if the whining 6.2-liter supercharged V8 wasn’t sonorous enough, the owner of this Dodge Charger SRT Hellcat wanted to make his ride sound even more brutal, so pops and bangs are on deck, and so is an ECU unlock, and a Stage 1 tuning kit, according to the quoted tuner.
The numbers haven’t been mentioned in the social media post embedded at the bottom of the page, but we know that this model came with upward of 700 horsepower in its most basic form, with superior versions having more than 800 hp available via the loud pedal. And since this isn’t exactly a dragster in disguise, even though it can likely pull an impressive performance in a quarter-mile battle, we likely won’t encounter it again.
Thus, before wrapping it up, we have to ask you whether you dig the makeover of this Dodge Charger SRT Hellcat . So, do you? View this post on Instagram A post shared by STARS IN THE CEILING (@stars.in.the.ceiling)

Subaru Recalls 2026 Crosstrek and Forester for Potential Control Arm Ball Joint Separation
52 photos
Photo: Subaru
The supplier that builds front lower control arms for the Subaru Crosstrek and Forester is to blame for this recall. Several finished assemblies were parked before the last step of the assembly process, namely the final torquing of the castle nut that secures the ball joint. The parts shipped anyway, prompting the company to issue a do-not-drive advisory.
Subaru's US subsidiary estimates that only eight such vehicles were shipped to dealers. The lower control arm in these vehicles locates the front wheel, letting it move up and down while keeping the wheel aligned with the rest of the suspension. Because of its shape, it's easy to understand that the ball joint acts as the pivot that lets the wheel travel over bumps and steer at the same time.
When that joint separates, the wheel is no longer properly connected, increasing the risk of a crash. Separating ball joints cause a loss of control, and you certainly don't want to experience that while driving at high speed on the freeway. Subaru claims there is no warning before the failure, hence the do-not-drive instruction.
Subaru of America explains in the recall filing published by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration that several left front lower control arm assemblies have been placed in the supplier's finished goods rack before the final castle nut torquing operation was completed. TOA of Indiana is the supplier in question.
Suspect assemblies were shipped to Subaru of Indiana Automotive in Lafayette, where both the 2026 model year Crosstrek and Forester are produced for the US market. As of October 2026, the Lafayette-based plant also makes the Ascent people carrier. To prioritize high-volume SUVs and localized electrification, three models shifted production to Japan.
Photo: Subaru The Legacy went the way of the dodo in 2025 due to decreasing customer demand for sedans, whereas Outback production was consolidated at the Yajima plant in Japan. The Impreza hatchback also moved to Japan, and who could blame Scooby for it? After all, both the Crosstrek and the Forester are way more popular in the United States by sales volumes.
Using supplier process records and vehicle traceability records, Subaru of America singled out eight potentially affected Crosstreks and Foresters. All were assembled for the 2026 model year between August 4, 2026, and August 13, 2026. The company learned about the issue after a field report. Dated September 15, 2026, the report describes a ball joint separation.
The very next day, Subaru of America workers at the Lafayette plant started inspecting castle nuts on all completed vehicles at the facility. Subaru of America then confirmed the reported vehicle had no recorded torque inspection pass result, and that missing record prompted further investigation.
Dealers have already been instructed to inspect and replace all potentially affected crossovers. The left front lower control arm ball joint assembly will be replaced at no charge whatsoever, and the new assembly promises to have a properly tightened castle nut. Customer notifications are expected by December 16, 2026.
Based on the same platform, the Crosstrek and Forester are both powered by four-pot boxers. Both can also be had as hybrids, and Subaru moves a lot of them. In year-to-date terms, the Crosstrek sold 138,249 units in the first nine months of 2026 as opposed to 156,476 examples for the larger Forester. The Outback is ranked third, clocking 104,759 deliveries through Q3 2026.

Small, but Mighty: This Compact Travel Trailer Is "Perfect for Spontaneous Adventures"
21 photos
Photo: Hobby Caravan
You know what they say about not needing to change anything about a good thing. If that good thing happens to be one of the quirkiest, surprisingly versatile, compact and lightweight travel trailers around, you can see why Hobby Caravans won't change much about it for 2027.
The Hobby Beachy has been around for five years now, after its debut as a concept in 2021. It's not a single travel trailer but an entire series of compact and light towables produced by storied German RV specialist Hobby Caravan and available throughout the Old Continent. As of this year, 2027 models are also available in the UK under the Aura brand .
The Beachy series is comprised of four floorplans that could, if you're feeling less generous today, be said to be just one with some variations. The idea behind them all is the same, that of offering a ready-to-go solution for instant adventures, equipped with the basics and none of the things you might not want, yet versatile and very convenient to use.
With the exception of the newer 420+ model, the other three Beachy models are very similar in specs and style, except for their size, which, admittedly, brings about certain limitations in terms of comfort and features. The Beachy 360 is the smallest of the lot and, as such, it has less space to work with than the others.
Photo: Hobby Caravan It's still a nice alternative to traditional tent camping. Beachy is designed for quick getaways to the beach, mountain, or wherever else you want, offering basic comfort in a package that remains essentially basic. It has a modular interior to rely on, which means you can either bring your own camping gear, go without, or use the available space for storage.
Beachy 360 is, as Hobby says, "small, but mighty" and "perfect for spontaneous adventures [because] everything you need on the road is onboard." "Everything" might be a bit of an overstatement, unless you understand by the word a shelter off the ground that you can fill with your own stuff.
That's not a con working against the Beachy 360, though, since it's intentional . This single-axle towable, built with vacuum-bonded sandwich panels, and styled in a deliberately minimalist, almost Mediterranean style, does not strive to be a home away from home. You can't fault it for lacking basic comforts when its goal isn't to offer them.
Photo: Hobby Caravan The Beachy 360 comes in at 5.08 meters (16.6 feet) of total length, with 3.66 meters (12 feet) in the body, 2.16 meters (7 feet) of width, and 2.67 meters (8.7 feet) of overall height. It's a double-entry unit like its siblings, so you have an extra-wide door on the campsite and a two-part tailgate-style door in the rear panel that's meant to encourage indoor-outdoor living.
The layout is the same one as across the entire Beachy series, with a face-to-face dinette and lounge at the back, a rudimentary kitchen at the front, and an angled closet that's emergency bathroom and storage all in one.
Storage options are fewer than in the larger units, but you still get two small pieces of furniture on either side, with open cubbies that you can equip with felt organizers and with elastic cables to keep your stuff in during transport. These felt organizers are optional, so they will cost extra, but you can add them to the other cubbies as well.
Photo: Hobby Caravan Even though the Beachy 360 is the smallest of the four floorplans, it can still be used as a sort of compact toy hauler. The table that goes into the rear dinette is not fixed, so you can fold it up and stow it away, freeing up floorspace for a pair of bikes, kayaks, or maybe even a slimmer motorcycle. You have four tie-downs standard for that, as well.
The dinette converts into a large double bed at night that will fit two adults and one child, but two adults traveling alone can also sleep on the twin beds without joining them. All the mattress inserts travel as backrests, which means you can use the space under the benches for more of your stuff.
Not that you'd really need to. The Beachy 360 also has overhead cubbies, and the large cabinet that will fit a porta-potty comes with more shelves and lots of hanging space.
Photo: Hobby Caravan The kitchen, if you can call it that, is a bare workspace with just a stainless steel sink and 39-liter (1.4 cu-ft) 12V cooler fridge inside a full-extension drawer with soft-close. You do get plenty of counterspace and a decent amount of storage, as well as power outlets, so you can bring your appliances of choice. Again, that's the whole point with a travel trailer like this one.
Construction on the Beachy 360 will be the same as with the other Beachy models. It sits on a KNOTT steel chassis with an overrun brake with automatic adjustment, extendable corner steadies, and a jockey wheel. It comes with double-glazed opening windows with integrated blinds and flyscreens. It has a 25-liter (6.6-gallon) tank for freshwater inside that storage closet and a rollable wastewater tank of an unspecified capacity.
Options range from the felt organizers to the aluminum storage box on the tongue , extra insulation, a bike rack on the drawbar, a 230V electric heater with 1kW output, and the porta-potti. The unit is prepped for solar, so you can take it off the grid for short periods by spending a bit more.
Photo: Hobby Caravan Hobby mentions an empty weight of 749 kg (1,651 lbs) for the Beachy 360, with a maximum permissible weight of 1,000 kg (2,204 lbs), upgradable to 1,200 kg (2,645 lbs) as an option. The figure for the empty weight is for reference only and will depend on your options .
The 2027 Beachy 360 starts at around €15,700-€17,000 before options, depending on dealer and the country you're from. That's roughly $17,600-$19,000 at the current exchange rate, and actually affordable for a three-person caravan in Europe, with the mention that this particular caravan lacks certain creature comforts that some would consider non-negotiables.
The second video below shows a 2025 model , but it should still serve because the 2027 brings little to no change.

Over the Hills and Far Away: 1984 Toyota Land Cruiser J60 Has Big Miles But Also Sensible Pricing
11 photos
Photo: Garage Kept Motors / Instagram
Sitting proudly in the inventory of Grand Rapids, Michigan-based Garage Kept Motors , this Copper Metallic and Beige/Tan 4WD Land Cruiser is ready to roll another 100k miles without breaking a sweat – or so we heard.
The Toyota Land Cruiser nameplate, alongside the Jeep Wrangler, Land Rover Defender, the Mercedes-Benz G-Class, and just a handful of others, is one of those models that are basically legendary no matter the angle you look at them or the generation you’re assessing. Born in 1951, the model has been in continuous production for no less than three-quarters of a century
As such, it has gained a proper cult following, and everyone has their favorites . If you’re an enthusiast of the J60 generation (the Station Wagon series) from the 1980s and early 1990s, then here’s a cool find for you. This is a 1984 Toyota Land Cruiser J60 packing a carbureted 2F straight six which “has that classic Toyota sewing machine sound,” dressed in brown and tan (actually Copper Metallic and beige) with a little over 101k miles on the odometer.
While other vehicles would be at the end of their life cycle at that point, the legendary resilience of the Toyota Land Cruiser promises that, with proper care and maintenance, this SUV is potentially ready for the next 100k miles of adventures and iconic memories. “A classic example of Toyota’s legendary four-wheel-drive utility, combining rugged capability with the practicality and comfort of a traditional SUV,” the FJ60 was purchased new in Texas and spent a decade in the Pacific Northwest and California.
“Benefitting from life in regions where vintage Land Cruisers remain particularly well appreciated,” the Copper Metallic over Tan SUV has an “unmistakable period-correct appearance that suits the character of this iconic 4x4,” and power comes from under the hood via a “proven” 4.2-liter inline-six-cylinder engine, paired with a 4-speed manual transmission.
There’s also four-wheel drive and a robust chassis, so this “Land Cruiser remains just as at home exploring a trail as it is cruising around town.” Most importantly, it has been “maintained with an extensive service history, providing documentation of its care over the years,” and there was an oil change over the summer and also a clean CarFax, it’s ready for “, and anyone looking for a vintage SUV with genuine utility.”
The pricing is quite sensible, too, as the dealership wants $36,900 to part ways with it. Meanwhile, a modern round-headlight 2027 Toyota Land Cruiser 1958 comes with a starting price of $58,180 sans destination and potential dealer hikes, and also a modern 326-hp i-Force Max hybrid powertrain featuring a 2.4-liter four-cylinder turbo engine and electric assistance.
